items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: See, when I worked at the Nest with Luis Russell, well, that was Charlie Johnson's band -- that was his second band.

ctx.x: Yeah, $84 a week, but we'd make almost that in tips sometimes. 75, 80. It depends on how they feel, you know. And then I stayed there. Then Charlie Johnson was the -- you see, we were supposed to be Charlie Johnson's second band because he was at Small's Paradise. And he got Luis Russell the job and Luis got the men.

And so that way -- and the funny part, one night I didn't understand the New York lingo with musicians at that time. So the boss came around -- he used to walk on the floors. He looked at me and said, "C'mon, boy, get off, get off, get off." So I thought he said get off the stand and I started packing my horn. He came back and said, "Where the hell you going?" I said, "I'm going home. You said get off." He says, "You dummy. I meant for you to take a chorus." He wanted me to jam a chorus. And everybody in the band…
